name: Alpha-Ketoglutarate (AKG)
summary: Alpha-ketoglutarate is an endogenous tricarboxylic-acid-cycle intermediate and co-substrate for multiple dioxygenases. It is marketed for longevity, but direct randomized human evidence for lifespan or broad anti-aging claims remains limited; widely cited biological-age findings are observational, uncontrolled, or multi-ingredient.
description: Canonical alpha-ketoglutarate research entity for evidence integration. Publication remains held while calcium-AKG versus AKG identity, biomarker validity, randomized aging outcomes, formulation differences, and long-term safety are reviewed.
primary_effects_or_targets: TCA-cycle metabolism; dioxygenase co-substrate activity; nitrogen metabolism; geroscience research
